### Best in class right now
**TPS7A0233PYCHR (TPS7A02 family)** — Texas Instruments. **0.41 mm² footprint** (0.64 × 0.64 mm, 4-ball DSBGA/YCH); 25 nA typical Iq (even in dropout), 200 mA max, 270 mV dropout at 200 mA, Vin 1.5–6.0 V, Vout 0.8–5.0 V fixed. Availability: Active/in production, stocked at DigiKey & Mouser (≈$0.83/1; ~$0.40 at 1k est.). **Why it wins:** It sits at the smallest practical LDO footprint (a 4-bump CSP ~0.64 mm square) *and* breaks the tie at that size with the lowest quiescent current in the class — 25 nA, roughly 10× lower than the other parts sharing the same 0.41 mm² footprint.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **TPS7A02** (Texas Instruments) — 0.41 mm² (0.64×0.64 DSBGA) — winner: smallest footprint *and* lowest Iq (25 nA).
- **AP7350** (Diodes Inc.) — 0.41 mm² (0.64×0.64 WLCSP) — exact footprint tie, but 250 nA operating Iq (20 nA standby) and 150 mA max; cheaper.
- **RP122** (Nisshinbo Micro Devices) — 0.41 mm² (0.64×0.64 WLCSP-4-P8) — footprint tie; trades nanopower Iq for higher load capability (not a low-Iq part).
- **ADP162** (Analog Devices) — ~0.9 mm² (4-ball, 0.5 mm-pitch WLCSP) — slightly larger; 560 nA Iq, 150 mA, very low noise.
- **NCP170** (onsemi) — 1.0 mm² (1.0×1.0 XDFN4) — larger footprint; 500 nA Iq, ultra-low noise/high-PSRR option when area is less critical.

### Comparison
| Part | Footprint (mm²) | Package | Iq (typ) | Iout max | Dropout | Vin / Vout | ~1k price |
|------|-----------------|---------|----------|----------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| **TPS7A02** (TI) | **0.41** | 0.64×0.64 DSBGA | **25 nA** | 200 mA | 270 mV @200 mA | 1.5–6.0 / 0.8–5.0 V | ~$0.40 |
| AP7350 (Diodes) | 0.41 | 0.64×0.64 WLCSP | 250 nA | 150 mA | ~120 mV @150 mA | 1.9–6.0 / 0.8–5.0 V | ~$0.25 |
| RP122 (Nisshinbo) | 0.41 | 0.64×0.64 WLCSP-4 | µA-class | 200 mA | low | to 5.5 V in | ~$0.20 |
| ADP162 (ADI) | ~0.9 | 0.5 mm WLCSP | 560 nA | 150 mA | ~140 mV | 2.0–5.5 / 0.8–5.0 V | ~$0.55 |
| NCP170 (onsemi) | 1.0 | 1.0×1.0 XDFN4 | 500 nA | 150 mA | 170 mV @150 mA | 1.7–5.5 / 0.8–5.0 V | ~$0.30 |

### Caveats
The three smallest parts (TPS7A02, AP7350, RP122) are an exact footprint tie at 0.64 × 0.64 mm (0.41 mm²) — the practical floor for a 4-bump WLCSP/DSBGA LDO — so the winner is decided on the Iq tiebreak, where the TPS7A02's 25 nA is decisive. The ~1k prices are estimates: I confirmed the TPS7A02 DSBGA as Active and orderable (DigiKey ≈$0.83/1) and the AP7350 WLCSP in stock at LCSC (≈$0.44 in small qty), but did not independently verify exact 1,000-piece pricing or confirm RP122's precise Iq from its datasheet. Note bare WLCSP/DSBGA parts are light-sensitive and demand fine-pitch assembly — if that's unacceptable, the smallest leaded fallback is the same TPS7A02 in 1.0 × 1.0 mm X2SON.

markdown:
### Best in class right now
**TPSM82823SILR** — Texas Instruments. **~12 mm² total solution size** built around a 5 mm² (2.0 × 2.5 × 1.1 mm) 10-pin µSiL module with the inductor integrated; only input/output ceramics (plus two feedback resistors) sit outside the module. Vin 2.4–5.5 V, Vout adjustable 0.6–4 V (covers 3.3 V), 3 A max, 4 µA operating Iq, 4 MHz switching. Availability: DigiKey (TPSM82823SILR), Active/in production, ~$2.00 at the 500-pc break (≈$1.8–2.0/1k); stock has fluctuated (0 to ~15k seen). **Why it wins:** integrating a 3 A converter *and* its inductor into a 5 mm² package, plus the 4 MHz switching that shrinks the external caps, gives one of the smallest complete 5 V→3.3 V footprints you can actually order today.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **TPSM82823SILR** (Texas Instruments) — ~12 mm² total solution — winner; smallest complete 3 A footprint, but adjustable-only (the fixed-Vout figure assumes no FB resistors).
- **TPSM82813SILR** (Texas Instruments) — ~7.5 mm² (MagPack) / 12 mm² (µSIP) module — sibling that adds frequency sync and lower output ripple and stretches Vin to 6 V, at slightly higher cost and a larger orderable (µSIP) package.
- **MPM3610AGQV** (Monolithic Power Systems) — ~15 mm² module (3 × 5 mm QFN) — only 1.2 A and needs external caps, but tolerates 4.5–21 V in if you ever need headroom above 5 V.
- **TPSM82913RDUR / TPSM82912RDUR** (Texas Instruments) — ~24.75 mm² module (4.5 × 5.5 mm QFN) — much larger; justified only when its integrated ferrite-bead low-noise/low-ripple filter and 17 V Vin are required.

### Comparison
| Part | Total solution / module | IC package | Integrated L | Iout max | Iq | Fsw | Vin | ~1k price |
|------|------------------------|-----------|--------------|----------|-----|-----|-----|-----------|
| TPSM82823SILR (TI) | ~12 mm² total | 5 mm² (2.0×2.5) | Yes | 3 A | 4 µA | 4 MHz | 2.4–5.5 V | ~$2.0 |
| TPSM82813SILR (TI) | 7.5–12 mm² module | 7.5/12 mm² | Yes | 3 A | 15 µA | 1.8–4 MHz | 2.75–6 V | ~$2.7 |
| MPM3610AGQV (MPS) | ~15 mm² module | 15 mm² (3×5) | Yes | 1.2 A | — | 2 MHz | 4.5–21 V | ~$2.5 |
| TPSM82913RDUR (TI) | ~24.75 mm² module | 24.75 mm² (4.5×5.5) | Yes | 3 A | — | 2.2 MHz | 3–17 V | — |

### Caveats
The winning **~12 mm² total-solution** figure is TI's number for the *fixed-output* configuration; the orderable TPSM82823SILR is adjustable, so two small feedback resistors add a fraction of a mm² — still the smallest in this set. Prices are taken from the 500-piece DigiKey break (true 1k tiers weren't displayed) and stock readings conflicted between sources, so treat availability as "orderable but verify live." For the shortlist I list module/package footprints rather than full verified BOM areas where TI/MPS don't publish a complete-solution number, so cross-part footprint comparisons below the winner are approximate.

name: Small buck converter, 12V → 3.3V
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**TPSM82903SISR** — Texas Instruments. **8.4 mm² package footprint** (3.0 × 2.8 × 1.6 mm 11-pin MicroSiP with fully integrated 1 µH inductor); 3–17 V input (meets ≥16 V), 0.4–5.5 V out at up to 3 A, 4 µA Iq, selectable 1.0/2.5 MHz. Needs only an input + output cap (and a feedback divider) to complete the design, so total solution stays in the mid-teens mm². Availability: Active/in-production, listed at Mouser, DigiKey, Arrow, Newark; DigiKey currently shows backorder (0 stock, ~20 wk lead at some sources) — confirm Mouser/TI stock. ~1k price ≈ $2.80–3.00. **Why it wins:** it packs the inductor *and* a 3 A synchronous buck into the same 8.4 mm² uSiP as TI's 1 A parts, giving the smallest total 12 V→3.3 V solution while still carrying real load and a 17 V rating.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **TPSM82903SISR** (Texas Instruments) — 8.4 mm² package — winner; most current (3 A) inside the smallest footprint, 17 V max.
- **TPSM82901SISR** (Texas Instruments) — 8.4 mm² package — same MicroSiP/footprint and 4 µA Iq, but only 1 A; pick it if your 3.3 V rail is light and you want the cheapest of the family.
- **TPS82150SILR** (Texas Instruments) — 8.4 mm² package — footprint tie, mature/proven 17 V 1 A MicroSiP; slightly thinner (1.5 mm) but older and 1 A only.
- **MPM3610AGQV** (Monolithic Power Systems) — ~15 mm² package — ~1.8× the area but a roomier 21 V input margin, 1.2 A, and the cheapest by far; the value pick when the extra Vin headroom matters.

### Comparison
| Part | Footprint (pkg) | Vin max | Iout max | Inductor | Iq | ~1k price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TPSM82903SISR (TI) | 8.4 mm² (3.0×2.8) | 17 V | 3 A | Integrated | 4 µA | ~$3.0 |
| TPSM82901SISR (TI) | 8.4 mm² (3.0×2.8) | 17 V | 1 A | Integrated | 4 µA | ~$2.5 |
| TPS82150SILR (TI) | 8.4 mm² (3.0×2.8) | 17 V | 1 A | Integrated | ~22 µA | ~$2.7 |
| MPM3610AGQV (MPS) | ~15 mm² (3×5) | 21 V | 1.2 A | Integrated | ~280 µA | ~$1.5 |

### Caveats
The headline 8.4 mm² is TI's quoted MicroSiP package/solution footprint; the true board area adds two small ceramics plus a feedback divider, so real total solution is roughly 12–16 mm² — still class-leading, and the three TI MicroSiP parts genuinely *tie* on the package metric (the 3 A TPSM82903 wins only because it does the most in that area). The biggest practical risk is the winner's 17 V rating: it clears the ≥16 V bar but leaves little margin on a noisy/automotive 12 V rail with transients, where the 21 V MPM3610 is safer despite the larger footprint. Both TPSM82903SISR and MPM3610AGQV-Z showed 0 DigiKey stock (backorder) at check time though both are Active — verify live stock (Mouser/TI, or the in-stock MPM3610AGQV-P variant) before committing, and treat the 1k prices as approximate.

name: Miniature load switch / power mux
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**GLF72101** — GLF Integrated Power. **0.77 × 0.77 mm 4-bump WLCSP ≈ 0.59 mm²** (0.4 mm pitch, 0.46 mm thick); Ron ≈ 31 mΩ typ @ 5.5 V, 2 A max, Vin 1.1–5.5 V (6 V abs-max), with True Reverse Current Blocking (TRCB) and output slew-rate control. Availability: DigiKey Marketplace, ~9,690 in stock, **~$0.13/1k**, Part Status: Active. **Why it wins:** It is the smallest footprint here while still carrying a full 2 A at a genuinely low 31 mΩ — nothing else combines a sub-0.6 mm² package with that current/Ron, and it adds reverse blocking + slew control that the comparably-sized TI parts lack.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **GLF72101** (GLF Integrated Power) — **0.59 mm²** (0.77×0.77 WLCSP) — winner; 31 mΩ/2 A plus TRCB and slew control in the smallest package.
- **TPS22916** (Texas Instruments) — **0.61 mm²** (0.78×0.78 WCSP) — essentially the same size, but higher Ron (60 mΩ typ @ 5 V) and no integrated reverse blocking; wins on ultra-low ~10 nA leakage.
- **TPS22910A** (Texas Instruments) — **0.81 mm²** (0.9×0.9 DSBGA) — older 2 A part; larger and higher Ron, kept here as a mature, widely-stocked alternative.
- **ADP195** (Analog Devices) — **1.0 mm²** (1.0×1.0 WLCSP) — has reverse-current blocking, but only >1 A and a narrower 1.1–3.6 V input; bigger than the leaders.
- **NCP451** (onsemi) — **1.26 mm²** (0.9×1.4 WLCSP6) — biggest of the group, but by far the lowest Ron (12 mΩ) and highest current (3 A) down to 0.75 V — the pick when Ron matters more than size.

### Comparison

|------|-----------|---------|-----------|-------|-----------|---------------|-----------|
| **GLF72101** | **0.59 mm²** | 4-WLCSP 0.77×0.77 | 31 mΩ @5.5V | 2 A | 1.1–5.5 V | Yes (TRCB) | ~$0.13 |
| TPS22916 | 0.61 mm² | 4-WCSP 0.78×0.78 | 60 mΩ @5V | 2 A | 1.0–5.5 V | No | — |
| TPS22910A | 0.81 mm² | 4-DSBGA 0.9×0.9 | ~85 mΩ | 2 A | 1.4–5.5 V | No | — |
| ADP195 | 1.0 mm² | 4-WLCSP 1.0×1.0 | 65 mΩ @1.8V | >1 A | 1.1–3.6 V | Yes | — |
| NCP451 | 1.26 mm² | 6-WLCSP 0.9×1.4 | 12 mΩ | 3 A | 0.75–5.5 V | No | — |

### Caveats
All of these are simple single-channel load switches, not 2:1 power muxes — a true integrated priority mux (e.g. TI TPS2116, ~2×2 mm) is meaningfully larger, so the "smallest" winner here is a load switch, not a mux. The GLF72100/72101 family shares one 0.77×0.77 package and datasheet; I confirmed GLF72101 as Active and in stock at DigiKey (~$0.13/1k) but did not independently verify 1k pricing for the TI/ADI/onsemi parts, and the TPS22910A Ron (~85 mΩ) is from secondary sources rather than a fetched datasheet. GLF's own datasheet PDF blocked direct download, so its specs are taken from GLF's product page and the DigiKey listing; the GLF72101 vs GLF72100 input-voltage floor differs slightly between GLF (1.1 V) and the DigiKey parametric (1.5 V).

name: BLE radio transceiver
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**EM9305** — EM Microelectronic. WLCSP23 with a **1.8 × 1.8 mm PCB footprint (~3.24 mm²)** — the smallest standalone BLE radio I could confirm as orderable. BLE 5.4 with LE Coded PHY; RX sensitivity −97 dBm @ 1 Mbps (−103 dBm @ 125 kbps coded); 3.1 mA RX / 3.4 mA TX @ 0 dBm (3 V), TX programmable to +10 dBm. Runs as a companion/co-processor IC over HCI to a separate host MCU (or standalone SoC). Availability: in production, orderable at DigiKey (WLCSP `EM9305BS211CS23B` ≈ $3.37/unit; QFN-28 `EM9305BU106LF28B` ≈ $3.27/unit). **Why it wins:** It is the most integrated genuine companion-radio on the market — a sub-3.3 mm² wafer-scale BLE 5.4 transceiver with HCI built into ROM — and still has competitive sensitivity and ~3 mA RX/TX current, so it beats every other co-processor on the size metric without compromising the secondary specs.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **EM9305** (EM Microelectronic) — **3.24 mm² (WLCSP23, 1.8×1.8 mm)** — winner; smallest, newest (BLE 5.4), best sensitivity/current of the group.
- **EM9304** (EM Microelectronic) — **4.37 mm² (WLCSP25, 2.09×2.09 mm)** — the proven predecessor; BLE 5.0, −94 dBm RX, TX to +6.1 dBm. Slightly larger and a generation behind, but same companion-IC/HCI architecture.
- **NXH3670UK** (NXP) — **7.03 mm² (WLCSP34, 2.45×2.87 mm)** — a true single-chip 2.4 GHz radio, but it runs a *proprietary* low-latency audio protocol (gaming headsets) with an embedded Cortex-M0, not general-purpose BLE host offload. In-category on size, off-category on function.
- **CC2564C** (Texas Instruments) — **64 mm² (VQFN, 8×8 mm)** — the classic dual-mode (BR/EDR + LE) HCI network controller for a separate host MCU; BT 5.1, RX to −93 dBm. Mature and robust, but ~20× the footprint, so it only wins where Classic BT is also required.

### Comparison
| Part | Footprint | Package | RX sens. (1 Mbps) | RX / TX current | BLE ver. / Coded PHY | ~1k price |
|------|-----------|---------|-------------------|------------------|----------------------|-----------|
| **EM9305** | **3.24 mm²** | WLCSP23 (1.8×1.8) | −97 dBm (−103 @125k) | 3.1 / 3.4 mA @0 dBm | 5.4 / yes | ~$3 (qty-1 $3.37) |
| EM9304 | 4.37 mm² | WLCSP25 (2.09×2.09) | −94 dBm | n/s (peak <12.5 mA) | 5.0 / yes | n/c |
| NXH3670UK | 7.03 mm² | WLCSP34 (2.45×2.87) | n/s | ultra-low (audio) | proprietary 2.4 GHz | n/c |
| CC2564C | 64 mm² | VQFN (8×8) | −93 dBm | n/s | 5.1 dual-mode / n/c | n/c |

### Caveats
Prices shown are single-unit DigiKey figures, not negotiated 1k pricing, which I could not independently confirm; treat them as order-of-magnitude. "Standalone radio" here means a part that runs the link layer/HCI for a separate host — the EM parts are dual-positioned (companion **or** SoC), and I ranked them as co-processors per the brief. The NXH3670 is included on footprint but is functionally a closed-protocol audio transceiver, not a general BLE host-offload radio, so it is not a true substitute; EM9304/CC2564C RX/TX current and CC2564C coded-PHY support were not stated in the sources I reached (marked n/s / n/c).

name: Wi-Fi transceiver
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**CYW43439KUBGT** — Infineon (AIROC, ex-Cypress). **13.98 mm² footprint (4.87 × 2.87 mm, 63-ball WLBGA, 0.4 mm pitch)**; single-band 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi 4 (802.11 b/g/n) FullMAC connectivity chip with integrated Bluetooth 5.4, host attach over SDIO or gSPI, integrated PA/LNA/T-R switch. Availability: DigiKey **Active**, 5,445 in stock, **~$4.21/1k**; also Mouser/Arrow. **Why it wins:** It is the smallest genuinely in-production Wi-Fi connectivity IC for an embedded host MCU — the radio in the Raspberry Pi Pico W — undercutting the classic 4×4 mm WF200 on area while remaining fully active and the cheapest of the group.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
1. **CYW43439** (Infineon) — **13.98 mm²** (4.87 × 2.87 WLBGA) — winner; Wi-Fi 4 + BT combo, host runs the TCP/IP stack (FullMAC), not a stack-offload NCP.
2. **WF200C / WF200D** (Silicon Labs) — **16 mm²** (4×4 QFN32) — the purest "Wi-Fi network co-processor" (no Bluetooth), but WF200C is **NRND** ("Not For New Designs"); use WF200D for new work.
3. **CC3301** (Texas Instruments) — **25 mm²** (5×5 QFN40) — only Wi-Fi **6** silicon here (+ BLE companion), bigger but newer-standard and host-TCP/IP friendly.
4. **Type 1YN / LBEE5KL1YN** (Murata, on CYW43439) — **35.8 mm²** (6.95 × 5.15 LGA) — smallest pre-certified *module*; trades bare-die area for a dropped-in, regulatory-certified RF design.
5. **ST67W611M1** (STMicroelectronics) — **~151 mm²** (12.28 × 12.28 LGA-32) — largest, but a true offload NCP: Wi-Fi 6 + BLE with on-module TCP/IP, TLS and Matter over a single SPI to the host.

### Comparison

|------|-----------|------|------------------|----------|----|-----------|
| CYW43439 | 13.98 mm² | IC (WLBGA) | Wi-Fi 4 b/g/n, 2.4 GHz | SDIO / gSPI | BT 5.4 | ~$4.21 |
| WF200C/D | 16 mm² | IC (QFN32) | Wi-Fi 4 b/g/n, 2.4 GHz | SPI / SDIO | none | ~$4.74 |
| CC3301 | 25 mm² | IC (QFN40) | Wi-Fi 6, 2.4 GHz | SDIO / SPI | BLE | n/c |
| Type 1YN | 35.8 mm² | Module (LGA) | Wi-Fi 4 b/g/n, 2.4 GHz | SDIO | BT 5.x | n/c |
| ST67W611M1 | ~151 mm² | Module (LGA-32) | Wi-Fi 6, 2.4 GHz | SPI / UART | BLE | n/c |

### Caveats
The ranking is pure die/module area: by that metric the CYW43439 wins, but note it is a FullMAC combo chip (host runs the network stack and it bundles Bluetooth), whereas the WF200 is the only "pure" stack-light Wi-Fi-only co-processor — and it now carries NRND risk on the WF200C ordering code. Footprints are taken from manufacturer datasheets/distributor parametric data; the 4.87 × 2.87 mm WLBGA figure for the '43439 appears consistently across Infineon/distributor listings but I could not extract it from the raw datasheet PDF directly. Prices marked "n/c" (CC3301, Type 1YN, ST67W611M1) were not independently confirmed at 1k and are omitted rather than guessed.

name: UWB transceiver
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**QM33110W** — Qorvo. WLCSP, **3.1 × 3.4 mm (≈10.5 mm²)** — the smallest production standalone IEEE 802.15.4z transceiver I could verify. Channels 5 (6.5 GHz) and 9 (8 GHz); HRP PHY at 850 kbps / 6.8 Mbps; single antenna port (TWR ranging, no PDoA), 2.4–3.6 V, optimized for coin-cell tags. Availability: in production, orderable at DigiKey/Mouser (sibling QM33120WTR13 ≈ $11 qty-1; 1k lower). **Why it wins:** identical die-scale footprint to the AoA part but a single RX path means the leanest BOM and lowest ranging power — exactly the "smallest footprint, then lowest power" target.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **QM33110W** (Qorvo) — 3.1 × 3.4 mm WLCSP (~10.5 mm²) — winner; single antenna, lowest-power TWR, no angle measurement.
- **QM33120W** (Qorvo) — 3.1 × 3.4 mm WLCSP (~10.5 mm²) — same footprint, adds PDoA/AoA (<5°) via a 2nd antenna port; marginally higher RX power for the extra path.

markdown:
### Best in class right now
**MSPM0C1104S8YCJR** — Texas Instruments. **1.38 mm²** footprint (8-ball DSBGA/WLCSP, 0.86 × 1.6 mm, 0.4 mm pitch) — roughly the size of an 0603 resistor and ~38% smaller than the next-smallest MCU. 24 MHz Arm Cortex-M0+, 16 KB flash, 1 KB SRAM, 6 GPIO, 12-bit 3-ch ADC, UART/SPI/I²C, 1-ch DMA, CRC-16, 5 V-tolerant I/O. Availability: DigiKey lists it **Active**, ~8,700 in stock, **$0.357 @ 1k**; also stocked at Mouser. **Why it wins:** Launched March 2025 as the explicitly marketed "world's smallest MCU," its sub-1.4 mm² die-size package beats every other orderable MCU on pure board area while still carrying a real ADC and the three standard serial buses.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **MSPM0C1104S8YCJR** (Texas Instruments) — **1.38 mm²** (0.86 × 1.6 mm, 8-ball) — the winner; smallest, but only 6 GPIO / 24 MHz / 1 KB RAM.
- **STM32C011D6Y6TR** (STMicroelectronics) — **2.41 mm²** (1.70 × 1.42 mm, WLCSP12) — ~75% larger area, but faster 48 MHz core, 32 KB flash, 6 KB RAM and more I/O.
- **MKL03Z32CAF4R** (NXP Kinetis KL03) — **3.22 mm²** (1.61 × 2.0 mm, WLCSP20) — older (2014) part; biggest GPIO budget here (~26 I/O), 48 MHz, 32 KB/2 KB.
- **ATSAMD11D14A-UUT** (Microchip SAM D11) — **4.56 mm²** (1.9 × 2.4 mm, WLCSP20) — largest of the group; 48 MHz, 16 KB flash, 4 KB RAM, adds USB if needed elsewhere in family.

### Comparison
| Part | Footprint (mm²) | Package | Core / Clock | Flash / RAM | GPIO | ~1k price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MSPM0C1104S8YCJR | **1.38** | 8-ball DSBGA | Cortex-M0+ / 24 MHz | 16 KB / 1 KB | 6 | $0.36 |
| STM32C011D6Y6TR | 2.41 | WLCSP12 | Cortex-M0+ / 48 MHz | 32 KB / 6 KB | ~10 | ~$0.60* |
| MKL03Z32CAF4R | 3.22 | WLCSP20 | Cortex-M0+ / 48 MHz | 32 KB / 2 KB | ~26 | ~$0.80* |
| ATSAMD11D14A-UUT | 4.56 | WLCSP20 | Cortex-M0+ / 48 MHz | 16 KB / 4 KB | ~20 | ~$0.80* |

### Caveats
Footprints are package body dimensions from manufacturer/distributor data (die-size CSPs, so the PCB land is essentially the body plus solder-ball spread); all four are 0.35–0.5 mm-pitch BGAs needing fine PCB/assembly capability, not hand soldering. Only the TI 1k price ($0.357, DigiKey) was directly verified — the ST/NXP/Microchip "~1k" figures (marked *) are approximations extrapolated from single-unit distributor pricing and should be re-quoted before design-in. The KL03 dates from 2014 and, while still orderable, carries the highest long-term-availability risk of the group; TI's MSPM0C1104 is the newest and the clear, uncontested winner on the size metric.

### Best in class right now
**STM32C011D6Y6TR** — STMicroelectronics. **2.41 mm²** package footprint (WLCSP12, 1.70 × 1.42 mm); Arm Cortex‑M0+ @ 48 MHz, 32 KB flash, 6 KB RAM, no radio (UART/I²C/SPI, 12‑bit ADC). Confirmed upstream: the `stm32c011` die is defined in Zephyr's `dts/arm/st/c0/stm32c0.dtsi` (STM32C0 SoC series support). Availability: in full production, ~60k stock at Future Electronics, ~$0.36 each at 5k (≈$0.40/1k). **Why it wins:** at 2.41 mm² it is the smallest *orderable* package among MCUs with genuine upstream Zephyr SoC support — edging the MAX32660 by a hair while being far cheaper.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **STM32C011D6Y6TR** (STMicroelectronics) — **2.41 mm²** (WLCSP12) — smallest footprint and cheapest, but a minimal M0+ (32 KB/6 KB, no radio) and no dedicated Zephyr *board* (SoC/dts support only).
- **MAX32660GWE+** (Analog Devices) — **~2.43 mm²** (16‑WLP, 1.55 × 1.57 mm) — effectively tied on size; vastly more capable (M4F @ 96 MHz, 256 KB/96 KB) and has a dedicated upstream board (`max32660evsys`), but ~5× the price.
- **nRF52805‑CAAA** (Nordic) — **6.10 mm²** (WLCSP, 2.48 × 2.46 mm) — only one here with a radio (BLE 5.2, M4 @ 64 MHz, 192 KB/24 KB); ~2.5× the footprint.
- **nRF52811‑CAAA** (Nordic) — **6.10 mm²** (WLCSP, 2.48 × 2.46 mm) — same die size as the 52805 with BLE 5.1 direction‑finding/LE Coded PHY; included to show the smallest *wireless* Zephyr option.

The top two are a statistical tie: STM32C011 WLCSP12 (2.41 mm²) vs MAX32660 16‑WLP (DigiKey lists 1.55×1.57 ≈ 2.43 mm², but ADI's datasheet states 1.6×1.6 ≈ 2.56 mm²) — within package-measurement tolerance, so a buyer prioritizing capability over ~0.8% area should treat the MAX32660 as co‑leader. name: Smallest easy-to-layout BLE MCU
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**DA14531** (DA14531-00000FX2 / -01000OG2) — Renesas (SmartBond TINY). **1.7 × 2.0 mm WLCSP17 ≈ 3.4 mm²** — the smallest production BLE SoC, and a complete radio needs only **6 external passives + a 32 MHz crystal + power**. Integrated buck/boost/bypass DC-DC PMU (no inductor in bypass off a 1.5 V cell), single-ended RF with a 3-element low-pass match, Arm Cortex-M0+, 48 KB RAM + OTP, ~240 nA hibernation. 2-layer layout is explicitly supported in Renesas' hardware guidelines. Availability: DigiKey, in stock, ~$1.85/1pc (WLCSP), volume noticeably lower. **Why it wins:** nothing orderable beats its footprint, and the 6-passive BOM with on-chip DC-DC means the whole radio fits on a cheap 2-layer board with one matching network — exactly the ranking metric.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **DA14531** (Renesas) — ~3.4 mm² WLCSP, 6 externals — the winner; tradeoff is ROM+OTP (no large embedded flash), so OTA designs usually add an external SPI flash.
- **nRF52805** (Nordic) — ~6.1 mm² WLCSP (2.48 × 2.46 mm), ~10 externals — purpose-built for 2-layer boards and has true 192 KB embedded flash, but ~2× the area and more passives than the DA14531.
- **DA14535** (Renesas) — ~6.6 mm² FCGQFN24 (2.2 × 3.0 mm), 6 externals — newer BLE 5.3 and the easiest to hand-lay-out (QFN, not WLCSP), pin-compatible with the 531; only the QFN is broadly stocked today, so it's bigger than the 531 WLCSP.
- **CC2340R2** (TI) — 16 mm² QFN24 (4 × 4 mm), integrated balun → single-ended 50 Ω — much larger, but trivially 2-layer-friendly, 256 KB embedded flash, <0.71 µA standby, and by far the cheapest (~$0.80 class).

### Comparison

| Part | Footprint (mm²) | Externals | Integrated DC-DC / match | Flash / RAM | Sleep | ~1k price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DA14531** (Renesas) | **~3.4** WLCSP | ~6 + xtal | Buck/boost/bypass; single-ended LPF | OTP+ext / 48 KB | ~240 nA | ~$1.3* |
| nRF52805 (Nordic) | ~6.1 WLCSP | ~10 + xtal | DC-DC; π-match | 192 KB / 24 KB | ~0.3 µA off | ~$2.0* |
| DA14535 (Renesas) | ~6.6 QFN24 | ~6 + xtal | Buck/boost/bypass; single-ended | OTP+ext / 64 KB | ~150 nA | ~$1.0* |
| CC2340R2 (TI) | 16 QFN24 | few + xtal | Integrated balun (single-ended 50 Ω) | 256 KB / 36 KB | <0.71 µA | ~$0.8* |

\*Volume estimates extrapolated from single-unit distributor pricing — see caveats.

### Caveats
1k pricing is estimated from confirmed single-unit DigiKey listings (DA14531 ~$1.85, nRF52805 ~$2.76), not independently verified at 1,000 qty. The DA14531/535 are ROM+OTP parts with no large embedded flash, so field-updatable (OTA) designs typically add an external SPI flash — a part the embedded-flash nRF52805 and CC2340R2 don't need; if you weight "fewest total externals incl. memory," that narrows the 531's lead. WLCSP on 2-layer is feasible but needs careful pad/via design; the QFN DA14535 and CC2340R2 are genuinely easier to route by hand despite larger area.

name: Smallest high-performance BLE MCU
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**NRF54L15-CAAA-R** — Nordic Semiconductor. **2.45 × 2.25 mm WLCSP-47 (≈5.5 mm²)** — the smallest footprint among genuinely high-compute BLE SoCs; 128 MHz Arm Cortex-M33 (DSP + FPU), 1.5 MB NVM, 256 KB RAM, TrustScale of TrustZone + CryptoCell-312 secure-boot, Bluetooth 5.4 with LE Coded PHY and Channel Sounding. Availability: DigiKey, in production, ~3,298 in stock, **~$2.60 @1k**. **Why it wins:** No other part pairs a 128 MHz Cortex-M33 with 1.5 MB/256 KB memory in a sub-6 mm² package — it is both the fastest and the smallest of the strong-compute field.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **NRF54L15-CAAA-R** (Nordic) — **≈5.5 mm² (2.45 × 2.25)** — winner: smallest *and* highest-clock (128 MHz) with the largest RAM/flash.
- **EFR32BG27C320F768GJ39** (Silicon Labs) — **≈5.98 mm² (2.3 × 2.6 WLCSP-39)** — nearly as tiny, but compute-light (76.8 MHz, 768 KB/64 KB, BLE 5.2); only edges the field on size if you relax the "high-performance" bar.
- **EFR32BG24B310F1536IJ42** (Silicon Labs) — **≈9.3 mm² (3.1 × 3.0 CSP-42)** — matches the winner's 1.5 MB/256 KB and adds an AI/ML accelerator + Secure Vault, but ~70% larger and only 78 MHz.
- **STM32WBA55CG** (STMicroelectronics) — **≈9.6 mm² (3.1 × 3.1 Thin WLCSP-41, approx.)** — 100 MHz, TrustZone, BLE 5.4, but half the RAM (128 KB) and a notably bigger die.

### Comparison
| Part | Footprint | Core / clock | Flash / RAM | Security | BLE | ~1k price |
|------|-----------|--------------|-------------|----------|-----|-----------|
| **NRF54L15-CAAA-R** | **5.5 mm²** | M33 @128 MHz, FPU+DSP | 1.5 MB / 256 KB | TrustZone + CryptoCell | 5.4, CS, Coded | ~$2.60 |
| EFR32BG27C320F768GJ39 | 5.98 mm² | M33 @76.8 MHz | 768 KB / 64 KB | TrustZone | 5.2 | ~$2 (est.) |
| EFR32BG24B310F1536IJ42 | 9.3 mm² | M33 @78 MHz | 1.5 MB / 256 KB | TrustZone + Secure Vault | 5.3/5.4 | ~$3 (est.) |
| STM32WBA55CG | ~9.6 mm² | M33 @100 MHz | 1 MB / 128 KB | TrustZone | 5.4 | ~$2.5 (est.) |

### Caveats
The EM9305 (EM Microelectronic) is physically smaller at 1.8 × 1.8 mm but is **disqualified** here: it runs a Synopsys ARC EM7D core (not a Cortex-M33) with little flash/RAM, so it cannot serve demanding M33/TrustZone firmware. The STM32WBA55 WLCSP-41 area (~3.1 × 3.1 mm) is approximate — I could not extract the exact mechanical figure from ST's datasheet (the PDF timed out) — and the BG27/BG24/WBA "@1k" prices are rough estimates, not confirmed distributor quotes (only the nRF54L15 price/stock was verified, at DigiKey). The nRF54L15-CAAA WLCSP is current production, not NRND.

markdown:
### Best in class right now
**ICE40UL1K-SWG16ITR50** — Lattice Semiconductor (iCE40 UltraLite). **1.40 × 1.48 mm 16-ball WLCSP (≈2.07 mm², 0.35 mm pitch)** — the smallest packaged FPGA in volume production. 1,248 logic cells (LUT4), 56 Kbit (57,344-bit) sysMEM EBR, 10 I/O in this package, and **NVCM on-chip non-volatile config → instant-on, single-chip** (no external flash). Availability: in stock at Mouser ~$3.30/1 (the SWG16 reel was discontinued at DigiKey, so qualify a second source); 1k pricing not independently confirmed. **Why it wins:** No other low-density FPGA ships in a footprint this small, and the UL1K packs the most logic of the SWG16-package parts while staying single-chip thanks to NVCM.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **ICE40UL1K-SWG16ITR50** (Lattice) — 1.40 × 1.48 mm WLCSP (~2.07 mm²) — winner; smallest package + most logic (1,248 LE) + NVCM instant-on.
- **ICE40UL640-SWG16ITR1K** (Lattice) — 1.40 × 1.48 mm WLCSP (~2.07 mm²) — identical package, NVCM; only 640 LE, but the most cleanly orderable of the family (~$1.31/1k via secondary listings).
- **ICE40LP1K-SWG16TR1K** (Lattice, iCE40 LP) — 1.40 × 1.48 mm WLCSP (~2.07 mm²) — same package, ~1,280 LE, but **SRAM config → needs an external SPI flash**, so not single-chip/instant-on.
- **GW1NZ-LV1CS16** (Gowin, GW1NZ) — 1.8 × 1.8 mm CSP16 (~3.24 mm²) — next-smallest; non-volatile (embedded flash), 1,152 LUT4 and far more RAM (72 Kbit BSRAM + 64 Kbit user flash), but ~56% larger footprint.

|------|--------------------|--------------|-----|----------------|--------|-----------|
| ICE40UL1K-SWG16 (winner) | 1.40×1.48 / 2.07 | 1,248 | 56 Kbit EBR | 10 | NVCM (non-volatile) | n/c (~$3.30/1) |

### Caveats
The three SWG16 parts are a **true tie on the ranking metric** — they share the identical 1.40 × 1.48 mm WLCSP body — so the winner was chosen on tiebreakers (most logic + single-chip NVCM); pick the UL640 if you want the cleanest stock, or the LP1K if you can spare an external flash. Availability is the main risk: the UL1K SWG16 reel shows as discontinued/0-stock at DigiKey while Mouser still lists it, so verify your distributor and second-source before committing. RAM bit-counts for the UL640 (28 Kbit) and the LP1K I/O/RAM figures come from family datasheets rather than the exact SWG16 part page, and 1k pricing for the WLCSP parts could not be confirmed from a primary distributor (the ~$1.3 figures are from aggregator listings).

name: Smallest high-capacity (strong) FPGA
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**Ti135F441** — Efinix (Titanium). **121 mm² (11 × 11 mm, 441-ball FBGA, 0.5 mm pitch)**; 132,192 logic elements, 480 DSP blocks, 9.83 Mb embedded RAM, 8-lane transceiver block (PMA up to 12.5 Gbps) with hardened **PCIe Gen4 x4**, hardened RISC-V, and an LPDDR4/4x x16/x32 controller — all on TSMC 16 nm. Availability: in production; listed at DigiKey/Mouser via Efinix, eval HW shipping (Sundance SMT135-C). ~1k price not publicly posted (request quote). **Why it wins:** among FPGAs that genuinely qualify as high-performance — six-figure LE count *plus* real multi-gigabit SerDes and hard PCIe Gen4 — nothing else puts that capability into an 11 × 11 mm footprint.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **Ti135F441** (Efinix) — **121 mm² (11×11)** — winner; 132K LE + PCIe Gen4 + 8× ≤12.5 Gbps SerDes in the smallest qualifying package.
- **Ti85F441** (Efinix) — **121 mm² (11×11)** — same tiny package and transceiver/PCIe Gen4 fabric but only ~83K LE; shows 11×11 mm is the floor for a transceiver-class Titanium, and Ti135 is the densest part there.
- **LAV-AT-X70…CSG841** (Lattice, Avant-X) — **195 mm² (15×13, chip-scale BGA)** — ~500K logic cells (~637K system LC) with up to 25 Gbps SerDes and hard PCIe Gen4: ~4× the logic and 2× the SerDes rate of the winner, but a larger package and longer lead times.
- **LAV-AT-E70…CSG841** (Lattice, Avant-E) — **195 mm² (15×13)** — same ~500K-LC die and package as the X70 but **no SerDes** (high-speed I/O + DDR4/LPDDR4/DDR5 only); the one part with confirmed distributor stock/price (~$696 @ qty 1, DigiKey, 52-wk lead).
- **Ti375…F529** (Efinix) — **361 mm² (19×19)** — 370,137 LE, 1,344 DSP, hardened RISC-V + PCIe Gen4; the heavyweight reference — much more logic, much bigger package.

### Comparison

| Part | Footprint (smallest pkg) | Logic | DSP | Transceivers / hard IP | Memory | ~1k price |
|------|--------------------------|-------|-----|------------------------|--------|-----------|
| **Ti135F441** (Efinix) | **121 mm²** (11×11, 441) | 132,192 LE | 480 | 8× ≤12.5 Gbps + PCIe Gen4 x4, RISC-V | 9.83 Mb + LPDDR4/4x | n/a (quote) |
| Ti85F441 (Efinix) | 121 mm² (11×11, 441) | ~83,232 LE | 300 | 8× ≤12.5 Gbps + PCIe Gen4 | ~6.2 Mb + LPDDR4 | n/a (quote) |
| LAV-AT-X70 (Lattice) | 195 mm² (15×13, CSG841) | ~500K LC | 700–1,800 | ≤25 Gbps SerDes + PCIe Gen4 | DDR4/LPDDR4/DDR5 | n/a (quote) |
| LAV-AT-E70 (Lattice) | 195 mm² (15×13, CSG841) | ~500K LC | up to ~1,800 | none (HS I/O + DDR only) | DDR4/LPDDR4/DDR5 | ~$696 @ qty 1 |
| Ti375…F529 (Efinix) | 361 mm² (19×19, 529) | 370,137 LE | 1,344 | SerDes + PCIe Gen4, RISC-V | 27.5 Mb + LPDDR4 | n/a (quote) |

### Caveats
The result hinges on how "high-capacity" is gated: ranked purely by die footprint, Efinix's transceiver-less Ti120 (123K LE, 13×13 mm/169 mm²) and the sampling-only Ti125 Edge (~123K LE, reportedly ~8×8 mm) are smaller still, but I excluded them as mid-range parts lacking SerDes/PCIe — if you only need logic-and-I/O, they (or the 3.5×3.4 mm WLCSP Ti60 at 62K LE) beat everything here on size. Lattice logic *cells* and Efinix logic *elements* are not directly comparable, and the Avant ~500K-LC figure (vendor "up to 500K," ~637K system-LC) plus its CSG841 = 15×13 mm dimension come from distributor/datasheet data I could not cross-check against a Lattice-hosted PDF (their selector guide and datasheet mirrors blocked direct fetch); SerDes lane counts on the smaller CSG841 Avant package are also likely a subset of the full-package maximum. Public 1k pricing was unavailable for the Efinix parts (quote-only), so only the Avant-E70's ~$696 qty-1 figure is distributor-confirmed.

### Best in class right now

- **2033900323 / 2033890323** (Molex Quad-Row, 32-pos) — **0.175 mm pitch, 0.6 mm height** — same winning architecture, just the lower circuit count; listed separately only because it's a distinct orderable density.

### Best in class right now
**SKY66409-11** — Skyworks Solutions. **1.25 × 1.7 mm 12-pin CSP = 2.13 mm²** footprint (0.35 mm height) — the smallest verified, orderable 2.4 GHz PA/FEM in this survey. Integrated PA delivers **+13 dBm** (up to +15 dBm max) for Zigbee/Thread/802.15.4 and **+10.5 dBm** EDR for Bluetooth; integrated LNA (2.5 dB NF typ.), T/R + bypass switches; **supply 1.8–3.6 V**, logic 1.2–3.6 V CMOS; 2.400–2.4835 GHz. Availability: **DigiKey — Active, ~3,093 in stock, ~$1.05/ea at 6k** (1k slightly higher). **Why it wins:** With the ranking metric being PCB area, its chip-scale package is ~40% smaller than the next FEM (PE562212, 3.24 mm²) and ~70% smaller than a 4×4 QFN, while still covering the full +13 dBm BLE/Zigbee power class needed for a coin-cell node.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **SKY66409-11** (Skyworks) — **2.13 mm²** (1.25×1.7 CSP) — winner; smallest footprint, but modest +13 dBm and thinner distributor stock.
- **PE562212** (pSemi / Murata) — **3.24 mm²** (1.8×1.8 LGA) — 52% larger, but much higher **+21 dBm** with 15 dB digital Tx gain control; distributor stock not independently confirmed (largely direct / Richardson RFPD).

- **nRF21540** (Nordic) — **16 mm²** (4×4 QFN16) — highest power here (**+21 dBm**) and easiest to design in, but the largest footprint by far; included as the high-power anchor.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SKY66409-11** | **2.13 mm²** | 1.25×1.7 CSP | +13 dBm (≤+15) | 1.8–3.6 V | 2.40–2.4835 GHz | ~$1.05 (6k) |

Per the brief, parts are ranked by PCB footprint first; all candidates are PA-integrated front-end modules (FEMs), since the smallest 2.4 GHz "PAs" in production are sold as PA+LNA+switch modules rather than discrete amplifiers. markdown:
### Best in class right now
**QPA9510** — Qorvo. **3.0 × 3.0 mm 16-pin QFN (≈9 mm²)**; +35 dBm P1dB (OP1dB ≈35.4 dBm), 34 dB gain with analog gain control, ~55% PAE, single 2.8–3.6 V supply, 100–1000 MHz (covers 433/868/915 in one part). Availability: DigiKey/Qorvo store, Active, ~$6.11/1k (low-volume DigiKey listing; ~23-wk lead). **Why it wins:** It sits at the same 9 mm² footprint floor as every serious sub-GHz PA, but inside that footprint it delivers the highest output power, the best efficiency, the widest band coverage, and the lowest (battery-friendly) supply — so nothing smaller does the job, and nothing its size does it better.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **QPA9510** (Qorvo) — 9 mm² (3×3 QFN) — winner; +35 dBm P1dB, 55% PAE, 100–1000 MHz, 3 V single supply.
- **GRF5510** (Guerrilla RF) — 9 mm² (3×3 QFN-16) — same footprint, slightly lower OP1dB (33.8 dBm) and narrower 0.88–0.96 GHz tuning; needs 5 V.

The footprint metric is effectively tied across all serious candidates: 3×3 mm (9 mm²) is the practical floor for this power class, since smaller QFN/DFN bodies can't dissipate ~+30 dBm of Tx heat — I found no in-production sub-GHz PA below this footprint, so the winner is decided on output power, PAE and band coverage within the 9 mm² tier. The QPA9510 PAE (~55%) and the SKY66423-11 P1dB are from manufacturer headline/marketing figures and should be confirmed against the datasheet at your exact bias and frequency; Guerrilla RF PAE was not stated on the pages I checked. Note the QPA9510 is described by Qorvo with legacy "GSM 900 MHz" language but is specified 100–1000 MHz and was repositioned (2025) as their wideband sub-1 GHz ISM PA, so verify the 433 MHz match and harmonic filtering for your design.

### Best in class right now
**BGA7L1N6** — Infineon. **0.77 mm² footprint** (TSNP‑6‑2 leadless, 0.7 × 1.1 mm) — by far the smallest orderable sub‑GHz LNA. NF 0.9 dB, gain 13.3 dB at 900 MHz; 728–960 MHz; VCC 1.5–3.3 V at only 4.4 mA; output internally matched to 50 Ω, needs 1 external SMD. Availability: in production/orderable (e.g. ~90k units stocked at Silitech, also Rutronik; LCSC carries its TSLP‑7‑1 sibling). **Why it wins:** at ~0.77 mm² it is roughly 1/5 the board area of every 2×2 mm DFN competitor while still delivering sub‑1 dB NF and double‑digit gain across the 868/915 MHz ISM bands.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
1. **BGA7L1N6** (Infineon) — **0.77 mm²** (TSNP‑6‑2) — smallest by a wide margin, but covers only 728–960 MHz (no 433 MHz) and NF/gain are mid‑pack.
2. **BGB707L7ESD** (Infineon) — **2.6 mm²** (TSLP‑7‑1, 2.0 × 1.3 mm) — next smallest; truly wideband (covers 433/868/915), current‑adjustable 2.1–25 mA, but higher NF (~1.1 dB) and lower gain (~15 dB).
3. **GRF2070** (Guerrilla RF) — **4.0 mm²** (DFN‑8, 2.0 × 2.0 mm) — 4× the area, but best‑in‑class NF (0.35–0.4 dB), ~21 dB gain, 0.01–1.7 GHz so it covers all three ISM bands.
4. **SKY67150‑396LF** (Skyworks) — **4.0 mm²** (DFN‑8, 2.0 × 2.0 mm) — same footprint as GRF2070, NF ~0.45 dB, ~19 dB gain, 300–2200 MHz, active and widely stocked.

The ranking metric is footprint, so the BGA7L1N6 wins decisively at ~0.77 mm² — but it tunes only 728–960 MHz, so **if your design must also serve 433 MHz it is disqualified**, and the smallest all‑three‑band part becomes the BGB707L7ESD (2.6 mm²), with the GRF2070 winning on noise if area is less critical. SiGe (B7HF). - **LFB152G45CB2D320** (Murata) — 0.50 mm² (0402) — winner; lowest IL at the smallest footprint, but weak low-band/cellular rejection.
- **2450BP07A0100001T** (Johanson Technology) — 0.50 mm² (0402) — ties on footprint; loses the tie-break on IL (2.5 dB) but gives more balanced 25 dB rejection across the 0.8–1.9 GHz cellular bands; 0.5 W, ~$0.17 @ 1k.

### Best in class right now
**SAFFW2G14AA0E0A** — Murata. **0.63 mm² footprint (0.9 × 0.7 × 0.55 mm)**; SAW Rx band-pass for LTE Band 1 (~2110–2170 MHz), unbalanced 50 Ω, in volume production. Availability: orderable through Arrow and JLCPCB/LCSC (the SAFFW family is stocked across bands); ~1k price not confirmed at time of writing. **Why it wins:** the SAFFW series is Murata's (and the industry's) smallest discrete cellular SAW filter at 0.9 × 0.7 mm — ~37 % less PCB area than the 1.1 × 0.9 mm parts every competitor still tops out at, while keeping conventional-grade insertion-loss/rejection across the 700 MHz–2.6 GHz LTE/FR1 bands.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **SAFFW2G14AA0E0A** (Murata) — **0.63 mm² (0.9 × 0.7 mm)** — winner; smallest orderable cellular SAW, full LTE band coverage in one footprint.
- **SAFFB1G84FL0F0AR1X** (Murata) — **0.99 mm² (1.1 × 0.9 mm)** — Band 3 SAW; previous-generation Murata footprint, more broadly stocked but ~57 % larger.
- **FAR-F6KA-2G1400-D4DW-Z** (Taiyo Yuden) — **1.40 mm² (1.40 × 1.00 mm)** — Band 1 SAW, IL 1.9 dB, very cheap, but marked *Not For New Designs* (NRND) and larger.
- **QPQ3501** (Qorvo) — **3.20 mm² (2.0 × 1.6 mm)** — BAW band-pass for n78; far bigger and aimed at base-station/small-cell power & rejection, not handset area savings.

### Comparison
| Part | Footprint (mm²) | Pkg (mm) | Type | Band | Insertion loss | ~1k price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SAFFW2G14AA0E0A | **0.63** | 0.9 × 0.7 | SAW | B1 Rx | ~1.5–2.5 dB (datasheet) | n/c |
| SAFFB1G84FL0F0AR1X | 0.99 | 1.1 × 0.9 | SAW | B3 | ~1.5–2.5 dB (datasheet) | n/c |
| FAR-F6KA-2G1400-D4DW-Z | 1.40 | 1.40 × 1.00 | SAW | B1 | 1.9 dB | ~$0.28 |
| QPQ3501 | 3.20 | 2.0 × 1.6 | BAW | n78 | low (BAW, base-station) | n/c |

### Caveats
Murata's SAFFW datasheet PDFs returned server errors during research, so the 0.63 mm² footprint and band assignment are confirmed (Murata product data + the 2019 "world's smallest SAW filter" announcement and distributor listings) but the exact per-MPN insertion-loss and rejection figures are not independently verified here — the ~1.5–2.5 dB range is typical for compact Rx SAW filters in these bands, not a quoted spec. TDK's TFSB thin-film band-pass filter is physically smaller (1.0 × 0.5 mm) but is an IPD part for 2.4/5 GHz WLAN/BT, not a narrow cellular SAW/BAW filter, so it is out of category; the Taiyo Yuden F6KA part is included only as a verified data point and is NRND. name: RF Filter — 5–6 GHz (Wi-Fi 5/6/6E)
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**6100BP14A1955001T** — Johanson Technology. **1.28 mm² footprint (EIA 0603, 1.6 × 0.8 mm, 0.65 mm max height)**; LTCC ceramic band-pass, single wideband passband 5170–7125 MHz covering the full Wi-Fi 5/6/6E UNII 1–8 range, insertion loss ~0.9 dB, rejects the 2.4 GHz and sub-5 GHz/cellular bands below and >7.5 GHz above. Availability: DigiKey, Active, ~2,120 in stock, **~$0.37 @1k** (17-week factory lead time). **Why it wins:** it is the smallest part that actually covers both the 5 GHz *and* 6 GHz Wi-Fi bands in one passband with sub-1 dB loss — smaller acoustic/LC parts exist but only reach the 5 GHz UNII band, so on the "smallest footprint that does the whole job" metric this is the leader.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **LFB155G50CB1B948** (Murata) — **0.50 mm² (0402, 1.0 × 0.5 mm)** — physically the smallest, IL 1.1 dB max, but passband is only ~5150–5850 MHz (Wi-Fi 5/6 5 GHz band); **does not cover the 6 GHz/6E band**, so it can't do the full-category job.
- **6100BP14A1955001T** (Johanson) — **1.28 mm² (0603)** — the winner; only sub-1 dB part covering the entire 5–7.125 GHz span.
- **5550BP14E0800001T** (Johanson) — **1.28 mm² (0603)** — same footprint, lowest loss of the group at 0.6 dB max, but passband 5150–5950 MHz only (no 6E 6 GHz coverage).
- **QPQ5601** (Qorvo) — **~2.21 mm² (1.3 × 1.7 mm laminate)** — largest here and 6 GHz-only (UNII 5–8, 5945–7125 MHz), but it's true BAW with steep skirts, high near-in rejection of UNII 1–3 and 28 dBm power handling — the pick when rejection/power beats area.

### Comparison
| Part | Footprint | Type | Passband (MHz) | Insertion loss | Rejection / power | ~1k price |
|------|-----------|------|----------------|----------------|-------------------|-----------|
| 6100BP14A1955001T (winner) | 1.28 mm² (0603) | LTCC LC | 5170–7125 (5/6/6E) | ~0.9 dB | Rejects 2.4 GHz & >7.5 GHz; power n/c | ~$0.37 |
| LFB155G50CB1B948 | 0.50 mm² (0402) | LTCC LC | ~5150–5850 (5 GHz only) | 1.1 dB max | 9.5 dB @4 GHz, 4.5 dB @7.5 GHz; 500 mW | ~$0.30 (est.) |
| 5550BP14E0800001T | 1.28 mm² (0603) | LTCC LC | 5150–5950 (5 GHz only) | 0.6 dB max | rejects 2.4 GHz; power n/c | ~$0.35 (est.) |
| QPQ5601 | 2.21 mm² (1.3×1.7) | BAW | 5945–7125 (6E only) | low (n/c) | high near-in UNII1–3; 28 dBm | ~$1.70 |

### Caveats
"Smallest footprint that covers the full 5 *and* 6 GHz band" drove the winner pick: the Murata 0402 (0.50 mm²) and Johanson 5550 (0.6 dB) are physically smaller or lower-loss but only pass the 5 GHz UNII band, so they're disqualified from full Wi-Fi 6E duty and listed as the better choice if you only need 5 GHz. The Johanson parts are wideband LC filters (they pass the whole 5–7 GHz band rather than separating 5 from 6 GHz), so use a Qorvo BAW (e.g. QPQ5601/QPQ5500) where steep 5/6 GHz coexistence rejection or high power is the real requirement. Insertion-loss figures are datasheet typ/max; exact 1k prices for the Murata and 5550 parts and power-handling for the Johanson parts were not independently confirmed at a distributor and should be checked before design-in.

markdown:
### Best in class right now
**RF1630** — Qorvo. **0.77 mm² footprint** (1.1 × 0.7 × 0.55 mm, 6‑bump WLCSP); SPDT, 100–6000 MHz, insertion loss 0.18–0.54 dB and isolation 42→22 dB across band, GPIO control, integrated DC blocking. Availability: orderable via Qorvo/RFMW, lifecycle "Production"; ~$0.26 at 1k (RFMW listed 0 in stock at time of check). **Why it wins:** No other in‑production 2.4 GHz‑capable switch we found packs an SPDT into a smaller PCB area, and it does so while keeping sub‑0.5 dB insertion loss through the ISM band.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **RF1630** (Qorvo) — **0.77 mm²** — smallest footprint; SPDT only and isolation falls toward ~22 dB at the top of its range, so it's a TX/RX or antenna‑select part, not a high‑isolation SP3T.
- **SKY13585-679LF** (Skyworks) — **1.00 mm²** (1.0 × 1.0 mm) — purpose‑built 1–6 GHz SPDT for WLAN; slightly larger and higher loss (0.95 dB max) than the RF1630.
- **SKY13586-678LF** (Skyworks) — **1.21 mm²** (1.1 × 1.1 mm) — native 2.4–2.5 GHz **SP3T** (extra throw) with 35 dB isolation; bigger, but the better pick if you need three ports / antenna diversity.
- **SKY13575-639LF** (Skyworks) — **2.56 mm²** (1.6 × 1.6 mm) — dual‑band matched **SP4T** Wi‑Fi switch; largest here, justified only when you need four throws and internal matching.

### Comparison

| Part | Footprint | Config | Insertion loss @2.4 GHz | Isolation @2.4 GHz | Freq range | ~1k price |
|------|-----------|--------|-------------------------|--------------------|------------|-----------|
| RF1630 | **0.77 mm²** | SPDT | ~0.2–0.5 dB | ~22–25 dB (band edge) | 0.1–6 GHz | ~$0.26 |
| SKY13585-679LF | 1.00 mm² | SPDT | 0.95 dB max | 20 dB min / 38 typ | 1–6 GHz | ~$0.40 |
| SKY13586-678LF | 1.21 mm² | SP3T | 0.75 dB typ | 35 dB typ | 2.4–2.5 GHz | ~$0.50 |
| SKY13575-639LF | 2.56 mm² | SP4T | 0.6 dB typ | high (matched) | 0.1–6 GHz | ~$0.80 |

### Caveats
The RF1630 is marketed for cellular (824–2170 MHz spec band) but its silicon operates to 6 GHz, so it covers 2.4–2.5 GHz; its band‑edge insertion loss/isolation at 2.4 GHz are interpolated from the datasheet curves rather than a discrete 2.4 GHz line item, and one distributor showed 0 stock despite "Production" status — verify lead time before committing. If you need a quoted‑at‑2.4 GHz spec or more than two throws, the Skyworks SKY13585/13586 are the safer "native" 2.4 GHz parts at a modest area penalty. The ~1k prices for the Skyworks parts are approximate (distributor quotes ranged widely by source) and should be confirmed at order quantity.

RFMW showed the RF1630 in production but at zero stock, so confirm current lead time before committing.

name: RF LNA — 400 MHz, low-power (Icc < 6 mA)
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**MAX2634AXT+T** — Analog Devices (Maxim). SC70-6, ~4.4 mm² (2.0 × 2.2 mm) with on-chip 315/433 MHz matching, so total footprint is essentially the IC plus 2–3 decoupling/DC-block 0402s; **NF 1.25 dB**, gain 15.5 dB, **Icc 2.5 mA typ (4 mA max)**, Vcc 2.2–5.5 V. Optimized for the 315 MHz and 433.92 MHz ISM bands, which bracket the 400 MHz target. Availability: in production and orderable at Mouser, DigiKey, LCSC and Richardson RFPD; LCSC lists ≈ $1.46 ea (low qty). **Why it wins:** it pairs the lowest qualifying noise figure with the smallest realizable footprint — its internal input/output match means there is almost no external matching network to add, unlike the wideband MAX2640, and it draws the least current of any qualifying part.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
1. **MAX2634AXT+T** (Analog/Maxim) — SC70-6 ~4.4 mm², NF 1.25 dB @ 2.5 mA — purpose-built for 315/433 MHz with internal matching; smallest total footprint and lowest current. *(winner)*
2. **MAX2640EUT+T** (Analog/Maxim) — SOT23-6 ~4.6 mm² body **plus an external L-C match**, NF ≈ 1.3 dB at 315 MHz (16 dB gain) @ 3.5 mA — broadband (300–2500 MHz) and proven at 315 MHz, but the added input/output matching network enlarges the total footprint and it draws ~1 mA more.
3. **MBC13720T1** (NXP) — SOT-363 ~2.5 mm², NF 1.38 dB @ 5 mA, 400 MHz–2.4 GHz — best raw footprint and a true 400 MHz part, but **NXP lists it as "no longer manufactured"** (NRND/obsolete), so it is excluded from the win on lifecycle grounds.

### Comparison

| Part | Footprint (LNA + match) | NF @ ~400 MHz | Icc (on) | Gain | Vcc | Freq coverage | ~1k price |
|------|------------------------|---------------|----------|------|-----|---------------|-----------|
| **MAX2634AXT+T** | SC70-6 ~4.4 mm², internal match | 1.25 dB | 2.5 mA (4 max) | 15.5 dB | 2.2–5.5 V | 315 / 433.92 MHz | ≈$1.46 (LCSC, low qty) |
| MAX2640EUT+T | SOT23-6 ~4.6 mm² + ext. L-C | ~1.3 dB (@315) | 3.5 mA | 15.1–16 dB | 2.7–5.5 V | 300–2500 MHz | not confirmed |
| MBC13720T1 | SOT-363 ~2.5 mm² + ext. match | 1.38 dB | 5 mA | ~17 dB | 2.5–3.0 V | 400 MHz–2.4 GHz | NRND/obsolete |

### Caveats
Neither winner specifies noise figure exactly at 400 MHz: the MAX2634 is characterized at 315 MHz and 433.92 MHz (1.25 dB), and the MAX2640's quoted ~1.3 dB is at 315 MHz — both bracket 400 MHz so the interpolated value is reliable, but the precise 400 MHz figure and the MAX2634's IIP3 were not independently confirmed. I could not read the MAX2634's typical-operating-circuit BOM directly (analog.com PDFs timed out), so the "minimal matching" claim rests on its RKE-targeted internal matching; verify the exact application-circuit components against the datasheet. Low-current LNAs from Guerrilla RF (GRF2100/2374, ≥6–8 mA), Skyworks and Qorvo were excluded for failing the hard <6 mA limit, and the MBC13720 was excluded as no longer manufactured.

name: Miniature 128 Mbit SPI NOR Flash
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**MX25U12843G** — Macronix. **16-ball WLCSP** (0.30 mm balls, 0.40 mm Z-height) — the smallest *package class* offered for a 128 Mbit SPI NOR, smaller in ball count and area than the 21-/24-ball WLCSPs from Winbond and Renesas and far below any SOP/WSON/USON. 1.65–2.0 V, Quad SPI / QPI, 133 MHz, –40 to +85 °C. Availability: Active part, orderable at DigiKey (P/N MX25U12843GBBI00), ~$3.56 @ 1k, though stock is currently constrained (0 on hand at DigiKey at time of writing). **Why it wins:** a 16-ball wafer-level chip-scale package is die-sized — the theoretical floor for PCB area — and is unambiguously smaller than the 9.0 mm² FO-USON8 and 9.94 mm² 21-ball WLCSP parts below it.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **MX25U12843G** (Macronix) — 16-ball WLCSP, 1.8 V — smallest package class; widest distribution of the chip-scale parts, but 1.8 V only and tight supply.
- **GD25LE128E (WLCSP 4×4 ball option)** (GigaDevice) — 16-ball WLCSP, 1.8 V, 120 MHz — same chip-scale class as the winner, modern small die; exact body dimension not independently confirmed and the WLCSP SKU is less widely stocked than the molded variants.
- **W25Q128JW** (Winbond) — 21-ball WLCSP, 1.8 V, 133 MHz — slightly larger ball array than the 16-ball parts; very well supported and second-sourced, the safest supply.
- **AT25QL128A** (Renesas/Dialog) — 21-ball WLCSP, **3.02 × 3.29 mm = 9.94 mm²** (confirmed), 1.7–2.0 V, 133 MHz — a hard, verified footprint number, but the largest of the WLCSPs here.
- **GD25LE128EXH** (GigaDevice) — **FO-USON8 3.0 × 3.0 mm = 9.0 mm²** (confirmed), 1.8 V, 120 MHz — the smallest *molded/leaded* part and the smallest footprint I could pin to a primary number; easier to hand-assemble than a WLCSP, but bigger than the chip-scale winners.

### Comparison

| Part | Footprint | Package | Interface | Max clock | Voltage | Temp | ~1k price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MX25U12843G | 16-ball WLCSP (smallest class; mm² not verified) | WLCSP, 0.30 mm ball | Quad SPI / QPI | 133 MHz | 1.65–2.0 V | –40/+85 °C | ~$3.56 |
| GD25LE128E (WLCSP) | 16-ball WLCSP (mm² not verified) | WLCSP 4×4 | Quad SPI / QPI | 120 MHz | 1.65–2.0 V | –40/+85 °C | n/v |
| W25Q128JW | 21-ball WLCSP (mm² not verified) | WLCSP | Quad SPI / QPI | 133 MHz | 1.7–1.95 V | –40/+85 °C | n/v |
| AT25QL128A | **9.94 mm²** (3.02×3.29) | 21-ball WLCSP | Quad SPI / QPI | 133 MHz | 1.7–2.0 V | –40/+85 °C | n/v |
| GD25LE128EXH | **9.0 mm²** (3.0×3.0) | FO-USON8 | Quad SPI / QPI | 120 MHz | 1.65–2.0 V | –40/+85 °C | n/v |

### Caveats
The exact WLCSP body dimensions for the three smallest candidates (Macronix MX25U12843G, GigaDevice GD25LE128E, Winbond W25Q128JW) are published only in package-outline drawings inside datasheet PDFs that my tooling could not render, so I ranked them by package *class* (16-ball < 21-ball < 24-ball WLCSP < molded) rather than a verified mm² — the two hard footprint numbers I could confirm are the 9.94 mm² 21-ball WLCSP (AT25QL128A) and the 9.0 mm² FO-USON8 (GD25LE128EXH). All five are current, Quad-capable 1.8 V parts; the winner is "Active" but supply-constrained (DigiKey showed 0 stock), so for a production design the Winbond 21-ball WLCSP is the lower-risk second source at a small area penalty. If absolute minimum area is non-negotiable, confirm the 16-ball WLCSP body size against the manufacturer's package drawing before committing, since I could not independently verify it.

name: Smallest FPGA with hardened PCIe
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**LFD2NX-28-7MG121C** — Lattice Semiconductor (Certus-NX). **36 mm² (6 × 6 mm, 121-ball csfBGA, 0.5 mm pitch)** — the smallest FPGA package that bonds out a *hardened* PCIe controller. Hardened PCIe **Gen2 x1** (SERDES to 5 Gbps), ~28K logic cells, on-chip EBR/LRAM (~2.6 Mb class), 18×18 DSP, ~1.0/1.2 V core. Availability: **In stock at DigiKey (479 pcs), $39.55/100** as tray; ~$30 est. at 1k. **Why it wins:** among FPGAs with a *built-in* PCIe endpoint/root block (not soft IP), no other part reaches a 6 × 6 mm footprint — the next hardened-PCIe option (CertusPro-NX at 9 × 9 mm) is more than 2× the area.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
- **LFD2NX-28-7MG121C** (Lattice, Certus-NX) — **36 mm² (6×6 mm)** — winner; PCIe Gen2 x1 only, modest ~28K LC.
- **LFCPNX-50** (Lattice, CertusPro-NX) — **~81 mm² (9×9 mm, smallest family pkg)** — steps up to hardened PCIe **Gen3** and 10G SERDES, but ~2× the footprint; PCIe bonding in the very smallest package needs confirmation (see Caveats).
- **LFE5UM5G-25F-8MG285C** (Lattice, ECP5-5G) — **100 mm² (10×10 mm, 285 csfBGA)** — mature/low-cost, hardened PCIe Gen1/Gen2 x1, 2× 5G SERDES; larger and older node.
- **MPF100T-FCSG325** (Microchip, PolarFire) — **121 mm² (11×11 mm, FCSG325)** — much more capable: hardened PCIe **Gen2 x4**, flash-based, but biggest of the small-package group.
- **Ti375C529** (Efinix, Titanium) — **BGA529, ~19×19 mm (~360 mm²)** — most capable by far (hardened PCIe **Gen4 x4** + RISC-V), but far larger; here only as the "if you need real PCIe bandwidth" reference.

### Comparison
| Part | Footprint (mm²) | Package | Hardened PCIe | SERDES | Logic (LC/LUT) | ~1k price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LFD2NX-28-7MG121C | **36** | 6×6 121-csfBGA | Gen2 x1 | to 5 Gbps | ~28K | ~$30 (est.) |
| LFCPNX-50 | ~81 | 9×9 (smallest) | Gen3 x1 | to 10 Gbps | ~50K | — |
| LFE5UM5G-25F | 100 | 10×10 285-csfBGA | Gen1/2 x1 | 2× 5 Gbps | ~25K | ~$15 (est.) |
| MPF100T-FCSG325 | 121 | 11×11 FCSG325 | Gen2 x4 | 4× 5+ Gbps | ~109K | — |
| Ti375C529 | ~360 | 19×19 BGA529 | Gen4 x4 | to 16 Gbps | ~370K | — |

### Caveats
Package areas are computed from nominal body dimensions (footprint = length × width), not solder-land area; the ranking is unaffected. The Certus-NX hardened PCIe Gen2 lane is confirmed present in the 6×6 mm 121-csfBGA for the LFD2NX-28/-40 SKUs (the -9/-17 lack the PCIe hard IP), and the winner is in stock at DigiKey. I could not independently confirm that CertusPro-NX bonds its PCIe SERDES in the "9×9 mm" package cited by Lattice's marketing — the readily orderable CertusPro-NX PCIe part is the larger BG484 — so its shortlist rank is provisional; likewise, 1k pricing for all but the winner is estimated, not quoted.

name: Smallest PCIe PHY
markdown:
### Best in class right now
**PI3EQX5801** — Diodes Incorporated (redriver / signal conditioner). **16 mm² (4.0 × 4.0 mm, 20‑TQFN)**; 1‑lane (2‑channel) PCIe 2.0 linear ReDriver, up to 5.0 Gbps, 3.3 V or 1.5 V supply, equalization + de‑emphasis. Availability: orderable at DigiKey/Mouser, **ACTIVE**; ≈$4.2 at distributor low‑qty (1k price not independently confirmed, likely lower). **Why it wins:** among genuinely *active, orderable* PCIe signal‑conditioning ICs it sits at the smallest footprint tier (16 mm²) while using the fewest pins (20) for a full single lane. It ties TI's SN65LVPE501 on area — see caveats.

Note on the two groups: **true discrete PIPE PHYs (group a) exist but are all obsolete** — no current-production part terminates the PCIe PHY layer for an external soft‑MAC. The only real parts (TI XIO1100, NXP PX1011B) are PCIe Gen1 and end‑of‑life. So the practical "smallest PCIe PHY" you can actually buy today is a **redriver** (group b), which is what the winner and most of the shortlist are.

### Shortlist (ranked by the metric)
1. **PI3EQX5801** (Diodes) — **16 mm²** (4×4, 20‑TQFN) — *redriver*, PCIe 2.0/5 Gbps; winner, but old generation (Gen2 only).
2. **SN65LVPE501** (Texas Instruments) — **16 mm²** (4×4, 24‑VQFN) — *redriver*, PCIe Gen1/2/5 Gbps, ACTIVE. Co‑leader on footprint; the RGET variant showed out‑of‑stock/no 1k price on TI at check time.
3. **DS160PR410** (Texas Instruments) — **24 mm²** (4×6, 40‑WQFN) — *redriver*, the smallest **modern PCIe Gen4 (16 Gbps)** part here, but 4‑channel (2 lanes), so larger footprint per part.
4. **NXP PX1011B** (NXP) — **81 mm²** (9×9, LFBGA‑81) — *true PIPE PHY* (8‑bit PXPIPE), PCIe Gen1 2.5 Gbps — **NO LONGER MANUFACTURED**; listed only to represent group (a).
5. **XIO1100** (Texas Instruments) — MicroStar BGA‑100 (size not independently confirmed) — *true PIPE PHY* (16‑bit TI‑PIPE), PCIe Gen1 — **OBSOLETE**.

### Comparison

| Part | Footprint (mm²) | Type | PCIe gen / lanes | Host interface | Supply | Status | ~1k price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PI3EQX5801** | **16** (4×4, 20‑TQFN) | Redriver | 2.0 / 1 lane, 5 Gbps | — (inline) | 3.3 V / 1.5 V | Active | ~$4 (low‑qty)* |
| SN65LVPE501 | 16 (4×4, 24‑VQFN) | Redriver | 1/2, 1 lane, 5 Gbps | — (inline) | 3.3 V | Active | not shown* |
| DS160PR410 | 24 (4×6, 40‑WQFN) | Redriver | 4.0 / 4‑ch, 16 Gbps | — (inline) | 3.3 V | Active | not shown |
| NXP PX1011B | 81 (9×9, LFBGA‑81) | True PIPE PHY | 1.x / 1 lane, 2.5 Gbps | 8‑bit PXPIPE | — | Obsolete | EOL |
| XIO1100 | BGA‑100 (unconf.) | True PIPE PHY | 1.1 / 1 lane, 2.5 Gbps | 16‑bit TI‑PIPE | — | Obsolete | ~$7 (hist.) |

\* Pricing not fully confirmable at 1k: the observed PI3EQX5801 figure (~$4.2) is distributor low‑quantity; TI's SN65LVPE501RGET showed no 1k price and out‑of‑stock at check time.

### Caveats
The two smallest active redrivers (PI3EQX5801 and SN65LVPE501) are a genuine **tie at 16 mm² / 4×4 mm**; I designated the Diodes part winner only on orderability and lower pin count, not a real size advantage. I excluded the Diodes **PI2DBS32212** (2.5×2.5 mm X1QFN, ~6.25 mm²) despite being smaller because it is a **passive 2:1 mux/switch, not a signal‑conditioning redriver/PHY** — it doesn't do the job this category asks for. True discrete PIPE PHYs (group a) are all end‑of‑life Gen1 parts, so if you need a buyable single‑lane PCIe front‑end today, a Gen2 redriver like the winner or a modern Gen4 redriver (DS160PR410) is the only realistic path; exact 1k pricing above could not be independently verified for several parts.
